rawContent.text: Jim Miller was the Chicago Bears’ quarterback in 2001. His regular-season line was 14 games, 13 starts, 228 completions on 395 attempts (57.7%), 2,299 passing yards, 5.8 yards per attempt, 13 touchdowns, 10 interceptions, a 74.9 passer rating, 11 sacks for 72 yards, and 29 rushing attempts for −19 yards and 0 rushing touchdowns. Biographical facts: James Donald Miller was born February 9, 1971, in Grosse Pointe, Michigan; he was 6 ft 2 in and about 225–226 lb; attended Michigan State; and was selected by Pittsburgh in the sixth round (178th overall) of the 1994 NFL Draft. The $2,000,000 signing bonus was reported for his subsequent five-year Bears contract agreed in March 2002, not as a 2001-season signing bonus. Sources: [Pro-Football-Reference](https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MillJi00.htm), [NFL.com](https://www.nfl.com/players/jim-miller/stats/), [ESPN](https://www.espn.com/nfl/columns/pasquarelli_len/1343738.html).
